page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8252C processor providing 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, containing 1,536 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering an allocation ratio of 32 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU hardware accelerators, directing all storage traffic across a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth connection.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptionally strong memory subsystem performance alongside moderate compute capacity. The instance scored in the top 25% for PassMark memory with a rating of 2,902.21, complemented by uncached large-block read throughput of 209.78 GB/sec and write throughput of 98.02 GB/sec. Geekbench compilation using Clang also demonstrated top-quartile performance at 40,125.0 points. Conversely, standard computational benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,561.0), Geekbench multi-core (13,330.0), and PassMark CPU (49,124.89) placed in the average middle tier. Due to the lack of dedicated acceleration hardware, token generation speed during LLM inference benchmarked in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a targeted investment for workloads bounded strictly by main memory capacity rather than raw compute scaling or ephemeral local disk speed. Because local storage is absent, data persistence relies entirely on network-attached storage architectures utilizing the 100 Gbps network interface. Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, high-capacity caching nodes, electronic design automation, and enterprise transactional systems requiring massive active data retention in RAM.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance configured with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8252C processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it provides an expansive 1,536 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering a 32 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU acceleration, depending on remote storage supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place its memory subsystem and uncached read/write bandwidth in the top tier, scoring 2,902.21 on PassMark memory and achieving 209.78 GB/sec in uncached read tests. General compute tasks, such as Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU, perform within the middle 50% percentile, while LLM text generation is restricted by the CPU-only profile. This instance is architected for large-scale in-memory databases, extensive caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise applications requiring immense RAM capacity.
